title: Amplitude of a sine graph
source: Theory P1-5.4 Quick check 1; amplitude of n sin x with n even

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: The coefficient of sine is \({n|int}\), so the amplitude is \({A|int}\).
steps.note: Amplitude is the positive coefficient of sine or cosine.

contexts.note: Includes the original y = 2 sin x

title: Period of sin nx in degrees
stem: State the period, in degrees, of \(y=\sin {n|int}x\).

steps.name: P
steps.text_tex: The period of \(y=\sin x\) is \(360^\circ\), so the period of \(y=\sin {n|int}x\) is \(\dfrac{{360^\circ}}{{{n|int}}}={P|int}^\circ\).
steps.note: Period of sin(bx) is 360 degrees divided by b.

title: Greatest value of a cosine graph after a vertical translation
source: Theory P1-5.4 Quick check 3; greatest value a + b
stem: State the greatest value of \(y={a|int}\cos x+{b|int}\).

steps.name: G
steps.text_tex: The greatest value of \(\cos x\) is \(1\), so the greatest value of \(y\) is \({a|int}\times 1+{b|int}={G|int}\).
steps.note: Add the vertical translation to the amplitude.

title: Graph of y = 3 cos 2x + 2 and related transformations

source.note: Stem verbatim from the official QP; marks from the official MS. Question number checked against the QP.

stem:
A curve has equation \(y=3\cos 2x+2\) for \(0\le x\le\pi\).

(a) State the greatest and least values of \(y\). [2]

(b) Sketch the graph of \(y=3\cos 2x+2\) for \(0\le x\le\pi\). [2]

(c) By considering the straight line \(y=kx\), where \(k\) is a constant, state the number of solutions of the equation \(3\cos 2x+2=kx\) for \(0\le x\le\pi\) in each of the following cases.

(i) \(k=-3\) [1]

(ii) \(k=1\) [1]

(iii) \(k=3\) [1]

Functions \(f\), \(g\) and \(h\) are defined for \(x\in\mathbb{R}\) by

\(f(x)=3\cos 2x+2\),

\(g(x)=f(2x)+4\),

\(h(x)=2f\bigl(x+\tfrac{1}{2}\pi\bigr)\).

(d) Describe fully a sequence of transformations that maps the graph of \(y=f(x)\) on to \(y=g(x)\). [2]

(e) Describe fully a sequence of transformations that maps the graph of \(y=f(x)\) on to \(y=h(x)\). [2]

steps.name: s1
steps.note: Official MS: B1, sight of 5.

steps.name: s2
steps.text_tex: (a) The least value \(-1\) is stated.
steps.note: Official MS: B1, sight of each value.

steps.name: s3
steps.text_tex: (b) The sketch is a curve, not straight line segments, showing one complete cycle starting and finishing at the candidate’s largest value.
steps.note: Official MS: *B1, needs to be a curve, not straight lines. One complete cycle starting and finishing at their largest value.

steps.name: s4
steps.text_tex: (b) One complete cycle starting and finishing at \(y=5\) and going down to \(y=-1\), and starting to level off at least at one end.
steps.note: Official MS: DB1.

steps.name: s5
steps.text_tex: (c)(i) \(0\) solutions.
steps.note: Official MS: B1.

steps.name: s6
steps.text_tex: (c)(ii) \(2\) solutions.
steps.note: Official MS: B1.

steps.name: s7
steps.text_tex: (c)(iii) \(1\) solution.
steps.note: Official MS: B1.

steps.name: s8
steps.text_tex: (d) Stretch by scale factor \(\dfrac{1}{2}\), parallel to the \(x\)-axis (or in the \(x\)-direction, or horizontally).
steps.note: Official MS: B1.

steps.name: s9
steps.text_tex: (d) Translation of \(\dbinom{0}{4}\) (or a translation \(4\) units in the positive \(y\)-direction).
steps.note: Official MS: B1. Accept translation/shift.

steps.name: s10
steps.text_tex: (e) Translation of \(\dbinom{{-\frac{{\pi}}{{2}}}}{{0}}\) (or a translation \(\dfrac{{\pi}}{{2}}\) units in the negative \(x\)-direction).
steps.note: Official MS: B1. Accept translation/shift.

steps.name: s11
steps.text_tex: (e) Stretch by scale factor \(2\), parallel to the \(y\)-axis (or vertically).
steps.note: Official MS: B1.

title: A cosine graph, the length of a chord, and intercepts of the chord

source.note: Stem verbatim from the official QP; marks from the official MS. Question number checked against the QP.

stem:
The equation of a curve is \(y=2\cos x\).

(i) Sketch the graph of \(y=2\cos x\) for \(-\pi\le x\le\pi\), stating the coordinates of the point of intersection with the \(y\)-axis. [2]

Points \(P\) and \(Q\) lie on the curve and have \(x\)-coordinates of \(\dfrac{{\pi}}{{3}}\) and \(\pi\) respectively.

(ii) Find the length of \(PQ\) correct to 1 decimal place. [2]

The line through \(P\) and \(Q\) meets the \(x\)-axis at \(H\,(h,0)\) and the \(y\)-axis at \(K\,(0,k)\).

(iii) Show that \(h=\dfrac{{5\pi}}{{9}}\) and find the value of \(k\). [3]

steps.name: s1
steps.text_tex: (i) The sketch is one complete cycle of a cosine wave, starting and finishing at a negative value.
steps.note: Official MS: B1, one whole cycle - starts and finishes at -ve value.

steps.name: s2
steps.text_tex: (i) The curve is smooth, flattens at the ends and the middle, and meets the y-axis at \((0,2)\).
steps.note: Official MS: DB1, smooth curve, flattens at ends and middle. Shows (0, 2).

steps.name: s3
steps.text_tex: (ii) \(P\left(\dfrac{{\pi}}{{3}},1\right)\) and \(Q(\pi,-2)\), so \(PQ^2=\left(\dfrac{{2\pi}}{{3}}\right)^2+3^2\).
steps.note: Official MS: M1, Pythagoras (on their coordinates) must be correct, OE.

steps.name: s4
steps.note: Official MS: A1, PQ = 3.7.

steps.name: s5
steps.text_tex: (iii) The equation of \(PQ\) is \(y-1=-\dfrac{{9}}{{2\pi}}\left(x-\dfrac{{\pi}}{{3}}\right)\).
steps.note: Official MS: M1, correct form of line equation or simultaneous equations from their P and Q.

steps.name: s6
steps.note: Official MS: A1, AG, condone x = 5 pi / 9.

steps.name: s7
steps.note: Official MS: A1, k = 5/2. SR: non-exact solutions A1 for both.
